name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-profile-duplicate-doctor
description: Names the second copy of a package your profile did not need. When a plugin lists a package the dsh installation already provides (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`) in its `dependencies`, pnpm materializes a real second copy inside `<profile>/node_modules`, that plugin imports the second copy, and a `unique symbol` the harness uses for module-level identity is evaluated twice: the agent loop's tool scheduler looks up `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` on the wrong copy of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, gets `undefined`, and every tool call in that profile dies — first-party ones included — with `dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`, `tool/call` already appended and `turn/end` closing immediately as an error (discussion #8287). This plugin scans the profile at boot and rescans whenever the profile changes while dsh is running — the window in which a plugin installed into a live profile can still be named, before the restart it makes fatal — comparing each entry under `<profile>/node_modules` against the copy the installation owns, reporting every entry that is a distinct second copy together with the manifest that declared it (its `dependencies` range and path), classifying harness packages as the identity-split class and everything else as a usually-harmless duplicate, and stating its own limits. One durable user-role advisory per agent names the same facts to the model, so a broken profile is diagnosed instead of retried. It does not remove the second copy and does not claim to: the real fix is upstream (`Symbol.for`, or resolving the package through the installation).
